source.title: Dharmakirti PV III Ground Truth Claims
source.author: Dharmakirti

source_span.quote: pratyaksa (perception) of particulars (svalaksana) is free from conceptual construction (kalpanapodha)

claims.claim_text: Perception of particulars is free from conceptual construction; reflexive or recognitional structure must not be smuggled into bare perception as a conceptual owner-substance.
claims.hetu: direct perception is defined as kalpanapodha
claims.sadhya: bare cognition does not require conceptual self-ownership
claims.vyapti_statement: If perception is defined as free from conceptual construction, then a theory of cognition may resist importing a constructed self or universal subject into perceptual givenness.

falsifier.condition: Show that Dharmakirti's kalpanapodha definition logically entails intrinsic self-manifestation or an enduring owner-subject.

claims.reasoning: This is a textual/formal axiom in Sanskritree, not a Lean-proved theorem. It supports the Buddhist candidate by blocking a quick move from perception to owner-substance.

source_span.quote: The particular is the ineffable object of perception

claims.claim_text: The directly perceived particular is ineffable and pre-conceptual; conceptual identity is not the same as perceptual givenness.
claims.hetu: svalaksana is the direct pre-conceptual object
claims.vyapti_statement: If particulars are directly given only pre-conceptually, then stable self-identity claims require additional constructive explanation.

falsifier.condition: Show that the direct particular itself contains a stable self-identity relation rather than only serving as a pre-conceptual object.

claims.reasoning: This gives the Dharmakirti candidate a source-backed route to no-self pressure without denying experience.

source_span.quote: x exists iff x has causal efficacy

claims.claim_text: Existence is tracked by causal efficacy; explanatory burden shifts from hidden essence to what cognition and objects do.
claims.hetu: to be is to have causal efficacy
claims.sadhya: cognition can be evaluated functionally rather than through substance metaphysics
claims.vyapti_statement: If being is tied to causal efficacy, then a cognition theory can ask what reflexivity does before positing what substance owns it.

falsifier.condition: Show a reflexivity phenomenon that cannot be given any causal/functional role but still must be counted as established within the Dharmakirti framework.

claims.reasoning: This supports a functional no-self interpretation. It is not enough by itself to explain manifestness.

source_span.quote: Pramana (Dharmakirti): valid cognition defined by arthakriya of its object

claims.claim_text: Valid cognition is tied to successful causal engagement with its object, not to disclosure by a permanent subject.
claims.hetu: valid cognition is defined through successful object-directed efficacy
claims.sadhya: validity does not require intrinsic self-manifesting subjecthood
claims.vyapti_statement: If pramana is grounded in successful object-directed efficacy, then epistemic validity can be reconstructed without invoking an enduring owner-subject.

falsifier.condition: Show that successful cognition is unintelligible unless cognition is intrinsically self-manifesting in Abhinavagupta's stronger sense.

claims.reasoning: Sanskritree flags this as coherentist/circular, so the claim is useful but capped.

source_span.locator: section 2.2.2 Dharmakirti's causal version of apoha
source_span.quote: anyapoha is there in the theory essentially to answer metaphysical worries

claims.claim_text: Dharmakirti's apoha explains conceptual grouping by exclusion without positing real universals; it is tied to causal chains from particulars through perception, thought, and word-use.
claims.hetu: conceptual grouping proceeds by exclusion of what is other
claims.sadhya: determination does not require a real universal or self-substance
claims.vyapti_statement: If conceptual determination works by excluding what is other, then shared identity can be explained without a real universal common essence.

falsifier.condition: Show that apoha requires a real universal or entails Nanavira-style transformation rather than only semantic/cognitive exclusion.

claims.reasoning: This is the missing first-class apoha claim. It strengthens Dharmakirti's no-universal account while keeping the Nanavira bridge at OVERLAPS because causal/semantic exclusion is not identical to Nanavira's transformation operation.
